entries.title: scikit-learn User Guide, 3.1 Cross-validation: evaluating estimator performance
entries.edition: scikit-learn 1.9 documentation (the release series g6[ml] installs; 1.9.1 when retrieved)
entries.published: 2026 (the 1.9 release series; the page's copyright line reads 2007 - 2026)
entries.jurisdiction: None: a statistical method, the same everywhere
entries.licence: BSD 3-Clause, as the page's footer states (BSD License); G6 stores only this citation, the hash and the clause reference.
entries.clause: Section 3.1, opening paragraphs: learning the parameters of a prediction function and testing it on the same data is a methodological mistake, so part of the data is held out as a test set; when settings are tuned, knowledge of the test set can leak into the model, so a test set is still held out for final evaluation and settings are compared by cross-validation on the training set (k-fold: a model trained on k - 1 folds and validated on the remaining one).

entries.title: scikit-learn User Guide, 3.1.2.2 Cross-validation iterators with stratification based on class labels
entries.edition: scikit-learn 1.9 documentation (the release series g6[ml] installs; 1.9.1 when retrieved)

entries.licence: BSD 3-Clause, as the page's footer states (BSD License); G6 stores only this citation, the hash and the clause reference.
entries.clause: Stratified splitters ensure that relative class frequencies are approximately preserved in each fold; StratifiedShuffleSplit (3.1.2.2.2) preserves the same percentage for each target class as in the complete set. The section's note: stratification can artificially shrink the spread of the metric across folds.

entries.title: scikit-learn User Guide, 12.2 Data leakage and 12.2.1 How to avoid data leakage
entries.edition: scikit-learn 1.9 documentation (the release series g6[ml] installs; 1.9.1 when retrieved)
entries.published: 2026 (the 1.9 release series; the page's copyright line reads 2007 - 2026)
entries.jurisdiction: None: a statistical method, the same everywhere
entries.licence: BSD 3-Clause, as the page's footer states (BSD License); G6 stores only this citation, the hash and the clause reference.
entries.clause: Data leakage, information not available at prediction time used in building the model, gives overly optimistic estimates; test data should never be used to make choices about the model. 12.2.1: always split the data into train and test subsets first, before any preprocessing; never call fit or fit_transform on test data; a pipeline performs each method on the correct data subset and is ideal for cross-validation and hyper-parameter tuning.

entries.title: scikit-learn User Guide, 3.4.4.4 Balanced accuracy score
entries.edition: scikit-learn 1.9 documentation (the release series g6[ml] installs; 1.9.1 when retrieved)
entries.published: 2026 (the 1.9 release series; the page's copyright line reads 2007 - 2026)
entries.jurisdiction: None: a statistical method, the same everywhere
entries.licence: BSD 3-Clause, as the page's footer states (BSD License); G6 stores only this citation, the hash and the clause reference.
entries.clause: Balanced accuracy avoids inflated performance estimates on imbalanced datasets: it is the macro-average of recall scores per class; it equals accuracy on balanced data, and drops to 1 / n_classes for a classifier above chance only because it exploits an imbalanced test set.

entries.rounding_note: The page prints its doctest values cut off, not rounded: 0.948 for 0.94861, 0.965 for 0.96543 and 0.908 for 0.90816.
entries.title: scikit-learn User Guide, 3.4.6.1 R2 score, the coefficient of determination
entries.edition: scikit-learn 1.9 documentation (the release series g6[ml] installs; 1.9.1 when retrieved)
entries.published: 2026 (the 1.9 release series; the page's copyright line reads 2007 - 2026)
entries.jurisdiction: None: a statistical method, the same everywhere
entries.licence: BSD 3-Clause, as the page's footer states (BSD License); G6 stores only this citation, the hash and the clause reference.
entries.clause: R2 = 1 - sum (y_i - yhat_i)^2 / sum (y_i - ybar)^2; a constant model predicting the mean scores 0.0, and the score can be negative; when the true target is constant the original definition is not finite (scikit-learn then forces 1.0 or 0.0 unless force_finite=False). Worked example: y_true [3, -0.5, 2, 7], y_pred [2.5, 0.0, 2, 8] gives 0.948.
